title: Peter Brown arrives on the Mayflower
description: Mayflower carpenter and a signer of the Compact; my direct ancestor.
subject: Mayflower;Colonial era;Literacy

title: Peter Brown's estate inventory lists a single Bible
description: His whole formal educational inheritance to his orphaned daughters.
subject: Colonial era;Literacy

title: Mary Brown marries Ephraim Tinkham
description: The marriage by which the family takes the Tinkham name.
subject: Colonial era

title: The Eliot Indian Bible is printed
description: Scripture translated into Wampanoag as an instrument of conversion and schooling.
subject: Wampanoag;Literacy

title: William Brenton 'purchases' Mattapoisett from Metacomet
description: The harbor 'bought' from the Wampanoag sachem (King Philip).
subject: Wampanoag;Land

title: King Philip's War; Middleborough disrupted
description: The Tinkham sons were early proprietors of Middleborough, which had no settled grammar school in their youth.
subject: Colonial era;Wampanoag

title: Rochester incorporated on the land called Sippican
description: The town founded on Wampanoag ground; later split into Marion and Mattapoisett.
subject: Colonial era;Wampanoag

title: Massachusetts district-school law
description: Towns divided into districts, each run by an elected prudential committee-man.
subject: District schools

title: Rochester adopts the district system (16 districts)
description: Grew to twenty-one districts by the 1820s.
subject: District schools

title: Rochester Academy built
description: Greek Revival academy at the town center; still standing.
subject: Academies

title: Mattapoisett Academy opens (later the Barstow School)
description: Private academy in the old 1816 Congregational meeting-house; became the Barstow School after 1870.
subject: Academies
image_alt_text: The Mattapoisett Academy (later the Barstow School), an 1816 meeting-house with a cupola, framed by bare trees.

title: Mattapoisett incorporated, separating from Rochester
description: Tinkhamtown becomes part of the new town of Mattapoisett.
subject: Local history

title: Thomas Tinkham sells the town a parcel for a district schoolhouse
description: At the elbow of Long Plain Road and Tinkham Lane; the land returned to the family after 1899.
subject: District schools

title: Tinkhamtown Chapel built
description: Conveyed 'only to be used for the worship of Almighty God,' on the site of a meeting house burned in 1850. (Group photograph ca.1890, courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum.)
subject: Local history
image_alt_text: A group of people, including several Tinkhams, in front of the Tinkhamtown Chapel, about 1890.

title: 'Three New Bedfords': the mills sort children by class
description: Mill schools, manual training, and the class divide a resident named that year.
subject: Mills

title: Center School opens (gift of Henry H. Rogers)
description: The 1899 building that anchored four generations of the family.
subject: Consolidation
image_alt_text: 1899 newspaper engraving of the new Center School building, with its clock tower.

title: Detail of Tinkhamtown, 1903 atlas of Mattapoisett
description: A 1903 map showing the school, chapel, sawmills, and Tinkham homes along Tinkham Lane.
subject: Local history;District schools
image_alt_text: Detail of a 1903 atlas showing the Tinkhamtown section of Mattapoisett, with a school, a chapel, sawmills, and several Tinkham family homes labeled along Tinkham Lane.

title: Great-aunt Ruthie leaves school to work in the mills
description: (approx., from the 1930 census) She left school so her brother Louis could stay; I carry her middle name.
subject: Mills

title: Oman Price graduates New Bedford High School
description: My paternal grandfather; later took extension courses at the Voke.
subject: Higher education

title: Marion graduates Fairhaven High School
description: Walked roughly three miles to the herring weir to catch the bus, then on to Kinyon-Campbell secretarial school.
subject: Consolidation

title: Louis enlists for WWII after New Bedford Vocational
description: (approx.) Lied about his age to enlist in the Army.
subject: Vocational;Mills

title: Louis earns a GI-Bill degree at the New Bedford Textile Institute
description: (approx.) Later taught engineering at the institution that became SMU / UMass Dartmouth.
subject: Higher education;Vocational

title: Old Rochester Regional High School opens
description: The shared tri-town high school; aunt Linda was in its first graduating class.
subject: Consolidation

title: Cyert Center for Early Education founded by women faculty
description: Begun with twelve children in a CMU dorm basement; my daughter Dorothea attends.
subject: Higher education;Childhood

title: Bent Twig alternative school opens in the Center School basement
description: Where my uncle Mark learned pennywhistle and carpentry (and the cherry-bomb story).
subject: Consolidation

title: My mother earns an MLIS at Drexel
description: (approx.) She became a public librarian; I earned the same degree about thirty years later.
subject: Librarianship;Higher education

title: Wopanaak Language Reclamation Project founded
description: Mashpee linguist Jessie Little Doe Baird begins reclaiming a language six generations without a speaker.
subject: Wampanoag;Literacy

title: I earn an MLIS at Drexel
description: The same degree, from the same school, as my mother.
subject: Librarianship;Higher education

title: My father earns a bachelor's at Northeastern at fifty
description: (approx.) Summa cum laude, graduating the same year I finished my degree.
subject: Higher education

title: I begin a doctorate at Teachers College, Columbia
description: In education; still in progress.
subject: Higher education

title: I become a faculty librarian at Carnegie Mellon
description: Teaching research and information literacy, like my grandfather and great-uncle taught.
subject: Librarianship;Higher education

title: West District ("Olive Branch") Schoolhouse
description: The West District Schoolhouse on Church Street, Mattapoisett, once called the Olive Branch Schoolhouse. Plate from Stiles, Mattapoisett and Old Rochester (1907).
subject: District schools
image_alt_text: A clapboard one-room schoolhouse behind a large tree.

title: Louis Reading with His Daughter
description: My grandfather Louis reading with my mother as a small child.
subject: Literacy
image_alt_text: A young man in a chair reading a magazine with a small girl on his lap, beside a vintage radio.

title: Minnie and Earl Tinkham
description: Minnie and Earl Tinkham in front of the house my parents live in today; Earl in his World War I uniform. (Date approximate.)
subject: Family
image_alt_text: A young man in uniform and a woman in a white dress standing in front of a clapboard house.

title: Tinkhamtown Schoolhouse
description: Photograph of the one-room Tinkhamtown schoolhouse. Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (0900.9.4).
subject: District schools
image_alt_text: One-room wooden schoolhouse with a small outhouse beside it.

title: Teaching Certificate, Tinkhamtown School
description: Certificate appointing Ethel W. Westgate teacher of the Tinkhamtown School for three months at $22 a month. Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (0500.3.495).
subject: District schools
image_alt_text: Ornate 1894 printed certificate appointing the teacher of the Tinkhamtown School.

title: "Indian Princesses, Massasoit's Kin" article
description: 1913 newspaper article on Teeweelema and her family's effort to keep their land at Lake Assawompset, framed in the period's romanticizing idiom. Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (0500.2.58).
subject: Wampanoag;Land
image_alt_text: 1913 newspaper page headlined "Indian Princesses, Massasoit's Kin, Live at Lake Assawompset."

title: Samp Mortar and Pestle ("Aunt Massy")
description: Wampanoag samp mortar and pestle associated with "Aunt Massy," a Native woman who lived and died at Capt. Nathaniel Hammond's house in the early 1800s. Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (1959.36.1).
subject: Wampanoag;Foodways
image_alt_text: A large carved wooden samp mortar and pestle.

title: Hammondtown School
description: Print of the Hammondtown school at River and Acushnet Roads, after a c.1869 painting by Clelia Lega Weeks; believed the oldest schoolhouse in town. Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (0900.9.17).
subject: District schools
image_alt_text: A small gable-roofed schoolhouse beside a dirt road, from a 19th-century painting.

title: Center School Classroom
description: Schoolchildren at their desks; the named roster mixes Yankee and Portuguese/Azorean families. Likely the Center School; the Museum record does not name the building. Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (0900.9.90).
subject: Consolidation
image_alt_text: About two dozen schoolchildren seated at wooden desks in a classroom.

title: Center School Desk
description: Oak two-student desk from the Mattapoisett Center School, possibly from the 1898-99 construction. Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (2021.1.1).
subject: Consolidation
image_alt_text: An oak two-student school desk.

title: Barstow School Classroom
description: Interior of a classroom in the Barstow School (the 1816 meeting-house that became Mattapoisett Academy, then the Barstow School in 1870). Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (0900.9.29).
subject: Academies
image_alt_text: Students in a 19th-century classroom interior.

title: Barstow High School Weekly Journal
description: Handwritten student newspaper of the Barstow High School, edited by Lemuel LeBaron Dexter, with subscriber lists, 1885-1886. Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (0500.2.131).
subject: Academies;Student media
image_alt_text: A page of a handwritten student newspaper.

title: Barstow School Report Cards
description: Report cards and entrance-exam marks for Lemuel LeBaron Dexter entering the Barstow School, 1884-1887. Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (0500.2.130).
subject: Academies
image_alt_text: Handwritten 1880s school report cards.

title: Mattapoisett District Schoolhouses
description: Copies of photographs of Mattapoisett's district schoolhouses before the 1899 consolidation. Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (0500.3.553).
subject: District schools
image_alt_text: A sheet of copied photographs of one-room schoolhouses.

title: Letter on School Distances
description: Letter to the Mattapoisett School Committee from Ansel Weeks listing road distances from the schoolhouse near Hammond's to other points in town. Courtesy of the Mattapoisett Museum (0500.3.554).
subject: District schools
image_alt_text: A handwritten 19th-century letter.

title: Birth Record of Joseph Louis Roberts Jr.
description: Massachusetts return of birth for my grandfather Louis, born at 78 Tallman Street, New Bedford; his father's occupation is recorded as eyelet maker. (Detail.)
subject: Mills
image_alt_text: A 1924 Massachusetts birth return listing the child's name, date, parents, and occupations.

title: Old Rochester Regional Senior High School
description: Old Rochester Regional, the shared high school for Mattapoisett, Marion, and Rochester, opened in 1961. (Photograph, 2007.) Mattapoisett Museum, 0900.9.63.
subject: Consolidation
image_alt_text: Color photograph of the brick entrance of Old Rochester Regional Senior High School.
